name: Custom output bit pattern / anti-theft pulse type
explain: Low byte holds rcv_Arg2 plus (bits1-2) the anti-theft pulse type (0=off,1-3=pulse styles); high byte is a 7-bit custom on/off pattern entered as a string of 1s/0s in the UI, used to drive an output (labelled 'Morse Code' in the app). GDriver independently describes this same high-byte field as a switch sequence that lets the rider clear or flip the controller's configured speed limit, and is explicit that it is a distinct field from the Flash-Save PIN, long write-lock password, and mobile-access password — though which controller profile treats the top bit and any special zero pattern as meaningful is left unresolved (effect unverified).
notes: 自定义输出模式 / 防盗脉冲:0-无效,1-防盗脉冲1类型,2-防盗脉冲2类型,3-防盗脉冲3类型 | Worthless: morseCode int field + fd_morse_code="Morse Code (0-127)" corroborates the high-byte 7-bit pattern (0-127) exactly; the low-byte anti-theft pulse type sub-field is not independently named in Worthless, so the register as a whole stays low (compound bitfield, address not verifiable).

name: Speed loop KP/KI gain pair
explain: Low byte is the proportional gain (SpeedKP) and high byte the integral gain (SpeedKI) of the closed-loop speed regulator; tunes how aggressively motor RPM tracks the commanded speed. GDriver corroborates the KP/KI split for controller profiles that use this stored speed-regulation loop, and adds that other controllers can derive, fix, or bypass the stored loop entirely, that gain too low leaves a lasting speed error, and gain too high causes hunting, surging, or instability (effect unverified — loop is only active on some control paths).
notes: SpeedKP/SpeedKI | SpeedKP / SpeedKI: label: SpeedKP / SpeedKI (no localized string in .cs)

name: Throttle low/high voltage threshold
explain: Low byte is the throttle signal voltage treated as zero throttle (0-2V), high byte the voltage treated as full throttle (2.5-5V); values outside the configured window are clamped. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address for both endpoints ('throttleLowVoltage'/'throttleHighVoltage'), and adds that a too-high low-point risks either an unsafe idle command or false throttle-loss detection, so both endpoints should be measured and calibrated together with margin for temperature and manufacturing drift.
notes: ThrottleLow/ThrottleHigh | ThrottleLow=油门低阈值(ProControlPage.cs:2156), ThrottleHigh=油门高阈值(ProControlPage.cs:2157)

name: Traction control enable / startup field-weakening word (FAIF)
explain: Bit 5 of the high byte enables Traction Control (TCS) per TCS_Clicked, toggled together with addr190/addr200; the same 16-bit word is also written wholesale by the Pro-mode FAIF field. GDriver independently treats FAIF as a combined register: one speed-change threshold bundled with several unrelated protection/control flags — among them something tied to sudden motor-RPM swings and Hall-sensor status — rather than a single traction-control strength dial, and warns that writing a partial value can silently flip a bit that has nothing to do with the value being tuned. This corroborates the official app's own wholesale-write behaviour, though the individual bit layout remains unconfirmed (effect unverified).
notes: TCS开启/关闭; FAIF | Worthless has a distinct `faif` int field confirming FAIF is a real firmware quantity, not a UI-only label; the TCS-enable sub-bit is not independently named in Worthless (fieldWeakening/cruiseEnable are separate, unrelated booleans).

name: Acceleration/deceleration curve response time
explain: Time constant for the throttle/torque ramp curve; larger values make acceleration and deceleration smoother (exact scale approximate, see CurveTime_TextChanged's num=val/2-1 transform). GDriver corroborates the millisecond framing but clarifies the controller actually counts a configured number of internal update calls between curve steps rather than running a free timer, so a bigger setting spaces the curve's steps further apart in real time; that mechanism is consistent with why this entry's displayed milliseconds are only approximate on some controllers (effect unverified).
notes: CurveTime | CurveTime=曲线采样(ProControlPage.cs:2117) | Worthless: curveTime int field + "Curve Time" label confirm name/semantics; no explicit range/scale recoverable statically (native).

name: Direction, brake response, park, NTC/PTC, anti-theft, phase-exchange config bits
explain: Packed configuration word written by many separate UI controls, each preserving the other bits: bit7=motor rotation direction, bits5-6=park mode (0=reverse-park,1=switch-park,2=disabled,3=slow-descent park), bits0-4=brake response mode, high-byte bits4-7(low nibble of low byte per NTC_PTC)=temperature sensor type, high-byte bit3=PC13/response mode, high-byte bit4=current anti-theft enable, low-byte bit7=phase exchange, high-byte bits0-2=slow-descent (steep hill) level (effect unverified). Worthless models direction, parkConfig, phaseExchange and brakeConfig as four separate top-level fields, corroborating that this really is a multi-purpose packed word matching the official bit breakdown; Worthless separately documents that two of the brake-response sub-field's values, 5 and 6, select distinct brake modes that turn on analog brake-lever input with an adjustable regen depth (one plain, one combined with park), refining but not fully resolving the bits0-4 brake-mode enum. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address for three of these packed sub-fields — 'motorDirection', 'phaseExchange', and 'temperatureSensorType' — matching the direction, phase-exchange and NTC/PTC bits above, and adds that motor-direction is 'not always equivalent to physically swapping two phase wires', while phase-exchange is instead a software-side current-sensor/output-channel swap that does not by itself reverse motor direction or correct every Hall/phase combination. GDriver also independently describes (by name match only, address unconfirmed) matching park-mode, brake-input, PC13, current-anti-theft, and slow-down-Park parameters consistent with this word's remaining sub-fields, including that PC13's role (drive-cutoff/cruise-on-ground-or-disconnect vs. a Normal/Race response-profile selector) is itself controller-design-dependent.
notes: 方向/驻坡/刹车/NTC_PTC/PC13/电流防盗/交换相线/陡坡缓降 combined register | Worthless: direction/parkConfig/phaseExchange/brakeConfig as separate fields + fd_brake_mode_hint enum values 5/6 (name+semantics match; full bit map and address not independently verifiable).

name: Motor phase/encoder angle offset
explain: Electrical angle offset applied between the encoder/Hall reading and the motor's true rotor position, used to correct phase alignment; no min/max clamp observed in the UI. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and describes it as the learned electrical angle that aligns rotor-position feedback with the controller's phase-current commands — an incorrect value can cause weak torque, rough/noisy running, high current, incorrect commutation, or motor faults, and it should be set only via self-learning or a known-correct value for the exact motor and wiring (effect unverified).
notes: PhaseOffset | PhaseOffset=相移(ProControlPage.cs:2084) | Worthless: phaseOffset Float field + "Phase Offset" label confirm name/semantics.

name: Zero-position ADC calibration coefficient
explain: The official app labels this field 'ZeroBattCoeff' (0电量系数, "zero battery-level coefficient") with a stored range of 768-1024, which earlier led this entry to guess the literal name was a misnomer for a throttle zero-point ADC calibration (grouped alongside addr8's throttle-voltage register). GDriver's own parameter registry directly contradicts that guess: it independently maps a same-address, same-range field ('zeroBatteryCoeff', minimum 768, maximum 1024) to this exact register and describes it at length as the lower endpoint of the controller's normalized battery-gauge (state-of-charge) calculation — calibrated from known battery voltages, distinct from throttle calibration (addr8's separate throttleLowVoltage/throttleHighVoltage fields), and explicitly warned not to be confused with the BMS or the controller's own low-voltage cutoff (addr31). Because this is a structural address-and-range match from an independent third app rather than just prose corroboration, the literal 'battery' name is very likely correct and this entry's earlier throttle-ADC theory is very likely wrong — confidence is nonetheless held at 'low' per this task's rule against raising confidence from GDriver evidence alone; see docs/decompile-notes.md for the full writeup.
notes: ZeroBattCoeff (label likely a misnomer for throttle ADC zero point) | ZeroBattCoeff=0电量系数(ProControlPage.cs:2119)

name: Full-position ADC calibration coefficient
explain: The official app labels this field 'FullBattCoeff' (满电量系数, "full battery-level coefficient") with a stored range of 1024-1536, which earlier led this entry to guess it was a throttle full-scale ADC calibration paired with addr13. GDriver's own parameter registry directly contradicts that guess: it independently maps a same-address field ('fullBatteryCoeff') to this exact register and describes it as setting when the controller's battery gauge reads full — noting regenerative braking may taper above roughly 95% charge depending on braking settings, and that the displayed voltage is only an estimate of full charge, not a guaranteed regen cutoff. As with addr13, this is a structural address match from an independent third app, so the literal 'battery' name is very likely correct and this entry's earlier throttle-ADC theory is very likely wrong — confidence is nonetheless held at 'low' per this task's rule against raising confidence from GDriver evidence alone; see docs/decompile-notes.md for the full writeup.
notes: FullBattCoeff (label likely a misnomer for throttle ADC full-scale point) | FullBattCoeff=满电量系数(ProControlPage.cs:2120)

name: Mid-speed current-loop KI/KP gain pair
explain: Low byte (MidKI) and high byte (labelled StartKI in one handler) tune the current-loop controller used around mid motor speed; the decompiled UI/variable names are inconsistent about which half is which. Worthless models midKI and startKI as distinct fields, and its auto-tune feature ("Resistance Scan") writes the same computed gain into all three of the Start/Mid/Max KI slots and derives each stage's proportional gain as ten times that stage's integral gain, corroborating that Start/Mid/Max-staged current-loop KI/KP gains are a real firmware concept. GDriver corroborates that MidKI and StartKI are both real, independent points on a Start/Mid/Max integral-gain schedule (not just a naming inconsistency) — too much gain causes roughness or instability, too little feels weak or slow — though it does not resolve which byte holds which value (effect unverified).
notes: MidKI/StartKI | label: MidKI / StartKI (no localized string in .cs)

name: Max-speed / startup current-loop KI/KC gain pair
explain: Low byte (MaxKI, range 1-24) and high byte (StartKC, range 1-16) tune the current-loop controller; the decompiled UI/variable names are inconsistent about which is which. Worthless models maxKI and startKC as two distinct fields, consistent with (but not resolving) the official code's own inconsistent cross-wiring of these two labels. GDriver treats MaxKI as the upper point of the same Start/Mid/Max integral-gain schedule, and describes the paired StartKC-labelled field as a 'stored starting KC' value that some controllers ignore entirely or derive from Starting KI instead — meaning a change to that half of this register may produce no observable effect on those controllers (effect unverified).
notes: MaxKI/StartKC | label: MaxKI / StartKC (no localized string in .cs)

name: Mid/Max KC current-loop gain pair
explain: Two related current-loop gain coefficients (MaxKC low byte, MidKC high byte per one handler, swapped in the other) packed into one register. Worthless: maxKC/midKC fields + "Max KC"/"Mid KC" labels confirm name/semantics. GDriver describes both as 'stored KC' fields that are not dependable independent adjustments: on supported control paths the controller may ignore the write outright, or instead compute the paired proportional term from its matching KI register, so on those controllers a change to either half of this KC pair can go entirely unnoticed by the rider — the precise byte order and which controllers actually use these values as written remain unverified.
notes: MaxKC/MidKC | label: MaxKC / MidKC (no localized string in .cs) | Worthless: maxKC/midKC fields + "Max KC"/"Mid KC" labels confirm name/semantics.

name: D-axis inductance (LD)
explain: Motor's d-axis winding inductance parameter used by the FOC current controller; units are not confirmed from the decompiled UI. GDriver independently reports that, despite the 'LD' name matching d-axis inductance, at least one FarDriver controller design actually treats this field as a 20-90 degree ceiling on the requested motor-current vector angle rather than a literal inductance value, with related controller designs said to use the field differently again — so this field's real physical meaning may not be a plain inductance on every controller (name match only, address unconfirmed; effect unverified).
notes: LD | label: LD (no localized string in .cs)

name: Fault alarm delay
explain: Delay before the controller reports a detected fault condition, used to filter transient glitches (effect unverified).
notes: AlarmDelay | AlarmDelay=告警延时(ProControlPage.cs:1755)

name: Motor pole pairs
explain: Number of magnetic pole pairs in the motor; used to convert between electrical and mechanical RPM. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and role, converting electrical rotation to calculated mechanical RPM (a larger entered count produces a lower calculated RPM for the same signal); it also independently notes that the pole-pair count only relabels the RPM axis GDriver shows for the drive-current/regen curves (addr136-155) without moving their stored breakpoints or changing commutation, current, or torque.
notes: PolePairs | PolePairs=极对数(PolePairsDisplay label, ProControlPage.cs:1561)

name: Maximum motor speed (high gear)
explain: Electrical RPM ceiling the controller enforces in high gear / full-speed mode. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and role as an RPM ceiling (not a guaranteed road speed), and adds that on some control paths the controller also uses this high-gear value when deriving linked Mid/Low-gear and Reverse-speed behaviour internally, so the four gear-speed registers (addr21/40-42) should be treated as a coordinated set rather than four independent caps.
notes: MaxSpeed / DHSpeed | DHSpeed=高速档速度(ParaPage.cs:6523 label), MaxSpeed=最大转速(ProControlPage.cs:1682)

name: Motor rated power
explain: Nameplate rated power of the motor, used by the controller for power-limiting calculations. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and role as a stored nameplate value only — it explicitly states this field does not act as the controller's output-power limit, and increasing it does not raise line current, phase current, torque, or top speed.
notes: RatedPower | RatedPower=额定功率(ProControlPage.cs:1563 label / 3563)

name: Battery rated voltage
explain: Nominal pack voltage class (e.g. 48V/60V/72V) the controller is configured for; affects protection thresholds and internal scaling. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and clarifies it is active calibration rather than a passive label — the controller uses it to normalize low-voltage protection (addr31) and other derived battery-state values (addr13/14, addr159), so an incorrect class can shift protection or gauge thresholds to the wrong real-world voltage.
notes: RatedVoltage / 额定电压

name: Motor rated speed
explain: Nameplate rated rotational speed of the motor, used as a reference point for the power/torque curves. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and adds that the stored value contributes to a voltage-coupled quantity the controller uses when shaping its high-speed drive-current curve during startup (see addr136-145) — it is not equivalent to the High-gear speed limit (addr21) and should not be inflated simply to chase a higher top speed.
notes: RatedSpeed | RatedSpeed=额定转速(ProControlPage.cs:1681)

name: Maximum battery (line) current
explain: Peak current the controller draws from the battery side, independent of motor phase current; protects the pack and wiring. Worthless names this field maxLineCurrent (Float) and labels it "Max Line Current" / "Hardware max current ceiling." — confirms name and role as a fixed hardware ceiling (as opposed to the separate Custom-override register, addr 38), but the explicit ×4-storage scale note in Worthless is documented only for the Custom-override fields (see addr 38/39), so it isn't independently applied here. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and role as the high-gear line-current request that the low/mid-gear percentages (addr50) are based on, and adds that it is a requested ceiling only — measured battery current can remain below the entered value once phase current, battery sag, BMS limits, temperature, and protections are applied.
notes: MaxLineCurr | DH=高速档力度(ParaPage.cs:6283 label), MaxLineCurr=最大线电流(ProControlPage.cs:2137)

name: Weak-field strength, speed-pulse count, follow/ECO/gear mode config
explain: Packed word: low-byte bits4-5=field-weakening strength (fast/middle/slow), low-byte bits0-1=follow-throttle mode, low-byte bits2-3=ECO throttle response curve (linear/sport/eco), high-byte bits0-4=speed-sensor pulse count (1-31), high-byte bits5-7=gear default mode; several separate UI controls all write this one register. GDriver's own parameter registry maps a 'speedPulses' output-configuration field to this same address, describing it as a value that is added into an internal pulse-output configuration rather than linearly multiplying the displayed speed — consistent with this being the high-byte speed-sensor-pulse-count sub-field, though GDriver does not expose the rest of this word's packing (effect unverified).
notes: 弱磁特性/速度脉冲/跟随/油门响应/档位方式

name: Q-axis inductance (LQ)
explain: Motor's q-axis winding inductance parameter used by the FOC current controller; units are not confirmed. GDriver independently reports that, despite the 'LQ' name matching q-axis inductance, at least one FarDriver controller design uses this field to form an upper and lower switching band around a live motor state rather than as a simple physical inductance number — so, like addr18/LD, the field's real physical meaning may differ from its name on some controllers (name match only, address unconfirmed; effect unverified).
notes: LQ | label: LQ (no localized string in .cs)

name: Battery rated capacity
explain: Nameplate amp-hour capacity of the battery pack, used for state-of-charge estimation. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and role, and explicitly notes the stored value is for identification/reporting only — it does not change the controller's current limits, unlock additional energy, override the BMS, or feed the controller's own battery-percentage (SOC) gauge calculation (addr13/14).
notes: BattRatedCap1 | BattRatedCap1=电池容量(ProControlPage.cs:2143)

name: Motor phase internal resistance
explain: Stator winding resistance value used by the controller's motor model / FOC estimator; units are not confirmed. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and adds an important caveat: the stored word also carries current-loop response selector bits alongside the resistance calibration, so it cannot be treated as one plain milliohm value — overwriting the whole register can change current-loop response as a side effect (effect unverified).
notes: IntRes | IntRes=电池内阻(ProControlPage.cs:1699 label -- Chinese label calls it 'battery' resistance despite being read alongside motor params)

name: Forward/reverse power ratio
explain: Percentage limit applied to output power/torque when the motor runs in reverse, relative to forward, per the official 'FwReRatio' label (后退齿比, literally "reverse gear ratio"). GDriver instead describes a matching field as a ratio applied to a speed-derived quantity (not a power/torque limit), using 64 as the internal full-scale reference on at least one control path, and explicitly states it is not the same thing as the Reverse-current ratio (addr201) or the Reverse-speed ceiling (addr41) — a materially different framing from this entry's original power/torque-percentage guess. Both readings remain unverified against a live controller (name match only, address unconfirmed); treat the power/torque-percentage framing with reduced confidence pending resolution.
notes: FwReRatio | FwReRatio=后退齿比(ProControlPage.cs:1756)

name: Low battery voltage protection threshold
explain: Pack voltage below which the controller cuts or limits power to protect the battery from over-discharge. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and adds that the stored threshold is recalculated together with Rated voltage (addr23), and that the precise path from this normalized value to an actual amount of current reduction or drive cutoff is not established across all controllers, so it should not be described as one universal trip voltage.
notes: LowVolProtect | LowVolProtect=欠压保护(ProControlPage.cs:3609)

name: Output relay / drive-mode feature enable bitfield
explain: 16-bit register where bits 0-10, 14 and 15 each toggle one single-bit output-relay or drive-mode feature (cruise, EABS, seat switch, auto-park, anti-theft, etc.) -- nearly every checkbox on the Para/Pro config pages targets one bit of this same word. ProControlPage.cs's RelayDelay_TextChanged is the one exception: instead of read-modify-writing a single bit like the other 21 handlers, it overwrites the *entire* 16-bit register (bits 0-15) with a raw numeric delay value, so this register also doubles as a plain relay-delay-time value in whatever mode that handler is used from; bit 15 (above) is a separate single-bit flag that is presumed to select the units (ms vs 1s) that value is interpreted in, but the two were not reconciled further. Worthless models autoBackP, gearRemember and assistRoll as separate booleans, consistent with the official bit-level breakdown of this packed relay/feature word; the remaining bits and the register's address are not independently verifiable. GDriver's parameter set independently corroborates the one-bit-per-feature framing with a long list of matching enable flags (cruiseEnabled, eabsEnabled, seatEnabled, autoBackProtectionEnabled, gearMemoryEnabled, reverseEnabled, overSpeedAlarmEnabled, pushAssistEnabled, forceTheftEnabled, parkDisableBrakeEnabled, among others), and notably includes a 'relayDelayOneSecondEnabled' flag whose name directly matches this entry's own speculation that bit 15 selects whether the RelayDelay_TextChanged raw value is interpreted in milliseconds or one-second units — though GDriver does not confirm the bit position or this register's address (effect unverified).
notes: 位0=坐桶/刹车灯(BC), 位1=坐桶开关(Seat), 位2=P档继电器(PGear), 位3=自动驻坡(AutoBackP), 位4=巡航(XH/Cruise), 位5=电子刹车(EABS), 位6=推行(Tuixing/freewheel), 位7=强制防盗, 位8=超速报警, 位9=驻坡禁刹车, 位10=记忆档位, 位14=后退使能, 位15=继电器延时单位(ms/1s选择, 单个bit). RelayDelay_TextChanged (bits 0-15, a raw delay value overwriting the whole register) is a separate, non-bitfield use of this same address -- 继电器延时(raw value, not a bit).

name: Save-config timestamp (write-only command)
explain: 6-byte year/month/day/hour/minute/second value written just before the save command (addr160 sub-command 4); records when parameters were last saved rather than a tunable setting.
notes: 保存时间戳

name: Custom maximum line current (secondary limit)
explain: The Boost mode's secondary battery-current (line-current) ceiling — a second, user-adjustable limit distinct from the primary MaxLineCurr register (addr25) that only takes effect while the assigned Boost input is active, providing a line-current ceiling above or alongside the normal High-gear setting. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and role (id 'customMaxLineCurrent'), replacing this entry's earlier 'likely a generic customer cap' guess with a specific Boost-path function; the ×4-scale note from Worthless (see notes) still applies.
notes: CustomMaxLineCurr | CustomMaxLineCurr=Boost线电流(ProControlPage.cs:2139) | CONFIRMED by Worthless: customMaxLineCurrent (Float, amps) + fd_override_current_desc="Override max current limits (stored as value×4 internally)" — ×4 storage matches official's scale=0.25 A exactly (same unit A, same width, compatible scale). Address agreement is NOT claimed (native-only).

name: Custom maximum phase current (secondary limit)
explain: The Boost mode's secondary motor phase-current ceiling — a second, user-adjustable limit distinct from the primary MaxPhaseCurr register (addr45) that only takes effect while the assigned Boost input is active. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and role (id 'customMaxPhaseCurrent'), replacing this entry's earlier generic-cap framing with a specific Boost-path function; the ×4-scale note from Worthless (see notes) still applies.
notes: CustomMaxPhaseCurr | CustomMaxPhaseCurr=Boost相电流(ProControlPage.cs:2140) | CONFIRMED by Worthless: customMaxPhaseCurrent (Float, amps) + fd_override_current_desc="Override max current limits (stored as value×4 internally)" — ×4 storage matches official's scale=0.25 A exactly (same unit A, same width, compatible scale). Address agreement is NOT claimed (native-only).

name: Low-gear speed limit
explain: Electrical RPM ceiling enforced when the vehicle is in low gear. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and role, and adds that the controller combines this value with Reverse speed (addr41) and High-gear speed (addr21) in its internal gear-speed scaling, so the gear-speed registers are a linked set rather than fully independent caps.
notes: LowSpeed | DL=低速档速度(ParaPage.cs:6683 label), LowSpeed=低速转速(ProControlPage.cs:1691)

name: Reverse-gear speed limit
explain: Electrical RPM ceiling enforced when the vehicle is driving in reverse. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address, and reports that on at least one control path this same value also feeds the controller's derived Mid- and Low-gear speed calculations — the lower-gear reference is scaled by (this value / High-gear speed, addr21) — so changing the reverse-speed limit alone can shift forward low/mid-gear behaviour on those controllers, not just reverse (effect unverified against a live device).
notes: BackSpeed | BackSpeed=后退转速(ProControlPage.cs:1711)

name: Mid-gear speed limit
explain: Electrical RPM ceiling enforced when the vehicle is in middle gear. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and role, and places it in the same linked gear-speed set as Low, High, and Reverse speed (addr21/40/41) rather than as a fully independent cap.
notes: MidSpeed | DM=中速档速度(ParaPage.cs:6603 label), MidSpeed=中速转速(ProControlPage.cs:1703)

name: Maximum deceleration rate
explain: Steepest allowed deceleration ramp the controller applies, e.g. releasing the throttle or braking; units/scale not confirmed. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and role: a bigger number generally pulls drive power down faster once the rider lifts off the throttle, though the felt result can still shift with motor RPM and whichever response mode is active, and this register does not itself set the regenerative-braking current (see addr48/49) (effect unverified — exact units/scale).
notes: Max_Dec | Max_Dec=减速灵敏度(ProControlPage.cs:2145)

name: Free/neutral throttle deadband
explain: Deadband applied around the throttle's released position to prevent creeping from a non-zero idle signal, per the official 'FreeThrottle'/电刹油门 ("electric-brake throttle") label. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address, but describes the field itself quite differently: an advanced value governing the transition between released-throttle coasting and release-throttle electronic braking, processed through multiple gated/scaled paths such that higher/lower values do not behave as a simple stronger-weaker deadband — a materially different framing from this entry's original deadband guess. Both readings remain unverified against a live controller; treat the deadband description with reduced confidence pending resolution.
notes: FreeThrottle | FreeThrottle=电刹油门(ProControlPage.cs:2118)

name: Maximum motor phase current
explain: Peak current the controller drives through the motor windings; the primary torque/power limiting parameter. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and role as the high-gear phase-current request underlying the low/mid-gear percentages (addr51) and the motor-current curve (addr136-155), and stresses it is a requested ceiling rather than a guaranteed telemetry value.
notes: MaxPhaseCurr | DH=高速档力度(ParaPage.cs:6283 label), MaxPhaseCurr=最大相电流(ProControlPage.cs:2138)

name: Analog speedometer / speed-sensor scale value
explain: Reference RPM value used to scale the analog speedometer output or an analog speed-limit input, depending on mode. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and role as an analog-speed-output calibration for compatible instruments, and clarifies it only changes the reported/displayed value — not actual motor RPM, road speed, or any of the controller's own speed limits — and should be adjusted only against GPS or another independent speed reference.
notes: SpeedAnalog | SpeedAnalog=模拟速度表系数(ProControlPage.cs:2150)

name: Maximum acceleration rate
explain: Steepest allowed acceleration ramp when the throttle is applied; units/scale not confirmed. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and role, and clarifies that it changes how quickly the controller ramps toward a larger drive-power request rather than raising the line- or phase-current ceilings themselves (addr25/45) (effect unverified — exact units/scale).
notes: Max_Acc | Max_Acc=加速灵敏度(ProControlPage.cs:2144)

name: Regen / stop-back current base level (energy feedback strength)
explain: Base coefficient for the selected regenerative-braking strength preset (Energy Feedback selector); also directly editable as StopBackCurr, described elsewhere as an anti-rollback current value. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address and role as a scaling factor applied to the controller's normal signed regenerative back-current request for a given brake command, consistent with this entry's anti-rollback/regen-strength framing.
notes: 能量回馈强度 / StopBackCurr

name: Regen / stop-back current secondary level

explain: Two adjacent bytes of the SEC0-SEC7 one-wire dashboard protocol timing table. GDriver describes SEC2 and SEC3 as two more slots in that same eight-byte one-wire rolling/encrypted-frame sequence, read and used to branch the controller's side of the paired-device handshake — not a display or motor setting in their own right (effect unverified).
notes: SEC2/SEC3 | label: SEC2 / SEC3 (no localized string in .cs)

name: One-wire comm protocol timing/section values 4-5
explain: Two adjacent bytes of the SEC0-SEC7 one-wire dashboard protocol timing table. GDriver describes SEC4 and SEC5 as further bytes in the same eight-byte sequence, each explicitly said not to be an independent current, torque, speed, or security-strength control (effect unverified).
notes: SEC4/SEC5 | label: SEC4 / SEC5 (no localized string in .cs)

name: One-wire comm protocol timing/section values 6-7
explain: Two adjacent bytes of the SEC0-SEC7 one-wire dashboard protocol timing table. GDriver adds a specific, concrete function for this pair beyond generic sequence data: SEC6 doubles as a bundled-profile-loading mode selector on supported controllers — raw value 2 loads the bundled profile selected by SEC7 during Save and startup, raw value 0 skips profile loading — while SEC7 selects which bundled profile number is loaded; that profile can reapply feature toggles, input assignments, switch behaviour, and other one-wire settings together (effect unverified).
notes: SEC6/SEC7 | label: SEC6 / SEC7 (no localized string in .cs) | Worthless models this as a single `oneCommSec: IntArray` field whose Kotlin default is `IntArray(8)` — matching the 8 SEC0..SEC7 values spread across these 4 registers (2 per register) exactly in count; scale/address not independently verifiable (native).

name: One-wire comm gear/output position nibbles (P/BC/Handlebar/FD)
explain: Four 4-bit nibbles (0-15) encoding the reported dashboard position/index for P-gear, side-stand (BC), handlebar and anti-theft (FD) states over the one-wire dashboard protocol. GDriver's parameter set independently matches this exact packing with four position fields sharing one word — a Park-status position, a side-stand-indicator position (confusingly named 'oneWireBrakePosition' in GDriver, values above 7 hiding the indicator), a throttle-active/working indicator position ('oneWireHandlebarPosition', despite the name), and an anti-theft-status position — confirming all four are purely display-status placements, not inputs or controls — and every one of the four positions has to line up with what the paired display expects, or the wrong status ends up shown (effect unverified).
notes: Ppos/BCPos/HBarPos/FDPos | Ppos=P位置/BCPos=边撑位置/HBarPos=转把位置/FDPos=防盗位置(ProControlPage.cs:1718-1721)

name: One-wire comm pulse count / square-wave high time
explain: Low byte = pulse count/divider (Pulse), high byte = square-wave high time (SQH) for the one-wire dashboard signal, per the official 'Pulse'/'SQH' labels. GDriver instead treats this pair as two generic auxiliary data bytes (A and B) in the one-wire protocol with a documented default of 0, explicitly stating they are not the communication pulse width, pulse period, or wheel-speed pulse count — a conflicting reading from this entry's original 'pulse/square-wave' framing. Both readings remain unverified; treat the specific byte roles with reduced confidence pending resolution.
notes: Pulse/SQH | label: Pulse / SQH (no localized string in .cs) | Worthless has a `pulseFD` int field, a tentative name match to this register's "Pulse" sub-field only (SQH sub-field not independently named).

name: One-wire comm line-current display coefficient
explain: Scaling coefficient applied to the line-current value reported over the one-wire dashboard protocol. GDriver confirms a matching 'OneLineCurrCoeff'-named field ('oneWireCurrentCoefficient') calibrates the current value reported over one-wire communication only — it does not raise the controller's actual line- or phase-current limits and cannot add motor power (name match only, address unconfirmed).
notes: OneLineCurrCoeff | OneLineCurrCoeff=电流系数(ProControlPage.cs:1722)

name: CAN bus speed, back-to-park delay and seat delay config
explain: Packed word: bits0-2 select CAN bus baud rate (250k/500k/1M), bits0-4 select a back-to-park delay time from a preset table (3s up to 300s or unlimited), bits5-7 select a seat-switch delay (1-7 units). GDriver's own parameter registry independently describes a matching CAN-baud-rate selector ('canBaud') with the exact same three options (250, 500, 1000 kbit/s), additionally noting the controller encodes them internally as raw values 8, 4, and 2 respectively — useful corroboration for this sub-field, though GDriver does not confirm this exact address or the back-to-park-delay/seat-delay sub-fields packed alongside it here.
notes: CAN速度/回P档延时/SeatDelay

name: Two-stage discharge: stage-2 SOC threshold
explain: State-of-charge threshold for the second stage of a two-stage battery discharge-limiting scheme; paired with Stage1Curr/addr158, per the register's naming and position — however, both the official app's own 'Stage2Soc' Chinese label (弱磁电流系数, "weak-field current coefficient") and GDriver's matching 'stage2Soc' parameter independently agree this is actually a field-weakening current coefficient, not a battery SOC threshold, despite the SOC-suggesting variable name shared by both apps. Treat the 'stage-2 SOC' framing as likely wrong; field-weakening coefficient is the better-supported reading (still low confidence — no address or scale confirmed by GDriver, and this task's rule bars raising confidence from GDriver help text alone).
notes: Stage2Soc | Stage2Soc=弱磁电流系数(ProControlPage.cs:1727 -- Chinese label describes it as a weak-field current coefficient, not obviously an SOC threshold; flagged as a possible label/behavior mismatch)

name: Under-voltage protection mode, current-limit way, TCS mode and ECO-acceleration level
explain: Packed word: low byte (0-12) selects the low-voltage protection style (fixed voltage drop, SOC percentage, or SOP value); high-byte low nibble is a current-limit-way selector (CurrLimitWay); high-byte high nibble selects the Traction Control (TCS) road-surface mode or the ECO acceleration level (1-8), depending on which UI control last wrote it. GDriver independently describes a matching 'CurrLimitWay'-named field ('currentLimitMethod') as selecting one of 13 numbered low-battery control profiles whose per-profile behaviour is not documented across the controller lineup, and confirms it leaves the ordinary maximum-current figure untouched on its own — consistent with this entry's high-byte-low-nibble CurrLimitWay sub-field (name match only, address unconfirmed).
notes: 欠压方式/TCS/经济加速/CurrLimitWay

name: Boost (overload) duration timer
explain: How long the controller allows a temporary current/power boost above the normal limit before reverting. GDriver independently describes a matching 'BstTime'-named field ('boostTime') as how long Boost stays on once a valid request comes in, with whole seconds as the unit on the controllers it supports, and stresses the value only governs that timing — the extra current/power comes from addr38/39 instead (name match only, address unconfirmed; effect unverified — exact seconds-per-count scale).
notes: BstTime | BstTime=Boost时间(ProControlPage.cs:1729)

name: Boost release/cooldown timer
explain: Cooldown period required after a boost event before another boost can be triggered. GDriver independently describes a matching 'BstRelease'-named field ('boostReleaseTime') as the Boost release/re-entry delay, again given in whole seconds on the controllers that support it, which the firmware tracks as its own internal countdown while it exits the boosted state and works back toward being armed for the next trigger (name match only, address unconfirmed; effect unverified — exact seconds-per-count scale).
notes: BstRelease | BstRelease=Boost释放(ProControlPage.cs:1730)

name: Park-mode engage timer
explain: Time the vehicle must be stationary before the park/anti-rollback function engages. GDriver independently describes a matching 'ParkTime'-named field ('parkTime') as the intended Park-control duration in seconds, which the firmware turns into a down-counter; once that counter runs out it is allowed to push the state machine toward Park or controlled-descent — but only once the mode, speed, brake, and switch conditions it also depends on line up, so simply raising this value does not by itself lengthen how long the bike must sit still (name match only, address unconfirmed; effect unverified — exact seconds-per-count scale).
notes: ParkTime | ParkTime=驻车时间(ProControlPage.cs:1731)

name: Inverse-time (I2t style) overload protection timer
explain: Time constant for an inverse-time overload curve, where higher overcurrent trips faster, per the official 'InverseTime' label (反向时间, literally "reverse time"). GDriver instead describes a matching field ('inverseTime') as one shared reverse/Park/controlled-descent response value that can shift both a state-transition threshold and a separate command ceiling at once, and is explicit that it does not behave like a plain timer — a substantially different reading from the inverse-time-overcurrent-protection framing above, and closer to the literal Chinese label's 'reverse' meaning. Both readings remain unverified against a live controller (name match only, address unconfirmed); treat the overload-curve framing with reduced confidence pending resolution.
notes: InverseTime | InverseTime=反向时间(ProControlPage.cs:1732)

name: Torque calculation coefficient
explain: Scaling coefficient the controller uses to convert current/FOC quantities into a torque command or display value. GDriver confirms a matching 'TorqueCoeff'-named field ('torqueCoefficient') calibrates this same calculated torque-related signal, and clarifies the controller divides the derived magnitude by this coefficient — so increasing it actually lowers the reported/calibrated torque value for the same underlying current, and it does not raise the motor's real torque ceiling (name match only, address unconfirmed; effect unverified — exact scale).
notes: TorqueCoeff | TorqueCoeff=扭矩系数(ProControlPage.cs:1728)

name: Throttle auto-learn: low (released) ADC value
explain: Raw ADC value captured during throttle auto-learn for the released position, per the official 'LearnVol' label. GDriver independently describes a matching 'learnVoltageLow'-named field as sharing its packed word with an additional, unrelated control bit used by the Rated-voltage (addr23) normalization path — meaning a naive whole-register overwrite can silently touch that unrelated bit alongside the learned ADC endpoint (name match only, address unconfirmed; effect unverified).
notes: LearnVol | LearnVol=自学习电压低(ProControlPage.cs:1738)

name: Throttle auto-learn: high (full) ADC value
explain: Raw ADC value captured during throttle auto-learn for the fully-open position, per the official 'LearnVoh' label. GDriver independently describes a matching 'learnVoltageHigh'-named field as sharing its packed word with several additional, unrelated control bits affecting motor-response hysteresis, a speed-limit override, acceleration/deceleration policy, and an alternate current-vector-angle path — meaning a naive whole-register overwrite can change far more than the learned ADC endpoint (name match only, address unconfirmed; effect unverified).
notes: LearnVoh | LearnVoh=自学习电压高(ProControlPage.cs:1739)

name: Park-mode speed-differential threshold
explain: Speed difference threshold used to decide when the park/anti-rollback control should intervene, per the official 'ParkDiff' label (缓降转速, "slow-descent speed"). GDriver independently describes a matching 'parkRpmDifference' field as the controlled-descent Park speed threshold, used by the controller alongside several nearby internal thresholds while changing states on the Park or slow-descent path — but cautions that nobody has confirmed the raw number equals actual motor RPM on every controller variant, and it is emphatically not one of the everyday riding speed caps (name match only, address unconfirmed; effect unverified).
notes: ParkDiff | ParkDiff=缓降转速(ProControlPage.cs:1733)

name: Sensorless/Isin startup angle parameter
explain: Startup parameter related to initial rotor-angle estimation (Isin) used before the motor is spinning fast enough for normal FOC (effect unverified).
notes: IsinStart | IsinStart=启动Is(ProControlPage.cs:1737)

name: Throttle-follow insert / TCS threshold configuration word
explain: Configuration word for the throttle-follow feature; bit5 is toggled together with addr9 when the TCS mode is changed, full field layout otherwise unconfirmed. GDriver independently confirms a matching 'ThrottleInsert'-named field ('throttleInsert') is a combined threshold rather than a single throttle-response or traction-control strength dial, and adds that the comparison the controller runs against it treats the field as signed when deriving an internal status/operating state — so a very large raw entry can flip sign and be read completely differently instead of just pushing the threshold further out (name match only, address unconfirmed; effect unverified).
notes: ThrottleInsert | ThrottleInsert=油门插拔(ProControlPage.cs:1761)

name: Throttle-follow exit speed and regen current ratio
explain: Low byte = speed at which throttle-follow/cruise disengages (FollowSpeed), high byte = a regen current ratio applied on release (ReCurrRatio, 32-255). GDriver independently confirms both sub-fields by name — 'followSpeed' as the RPM threshold for leaving low-speed creep (not the bike's normal speed limit), and 'reverseCurrentRatio' as a multiplier the controller applies to the reverse current-command relative to a 128-count full scale — which is consistent with this entry's 32-255 range being a fraction of that same 128-based scale (name match only, address unconfirmed).
notes: FollowSpeed/ReCurrRatio | FollowSpeed=跟随转速(ProControlPage.cs:1762), ReCurrRatio=后退电流比(ProControlPage.cs:1763) | Worthless: reCurrRatio (name match to ReCurrRatio) and a separate exitFollowSpeed field (tentative match to FollowSpeed, not certain given official's own note that FollowSpeed's exact sub-field is unclear).

name: Angle-learn state, speed-limit-pin and repair-pin selection
explain: Low byte = angle-learn status/result byte; high byte packs the speed-limit input pin selection (low nibble) and one-key-repair input pin selection (high nibble). Worthless models angleLearn and spdLmtSel as two separate fields, corroborating the official note that this register packs angle-learn and speed-limit-source selection together.
notes: anglelearn/限速Pin/一键修复Pin

name: High/low-speed switch mode, temp-70 level, long-back, no-CAN timeout, throttle-lost alarm
explain: Low byte = no-CAN-signal timeout (in 10s units); high byte bits0-3 = high/low speed switch mode (SPModeConfig, 0-15), bits4-5 = a 'Temp70' threshold level, bit6 = long-press-for-reverse enable, bit7 = throttle-lost alarm enable. Worthless models spMode, temp70, longBack, throttleLostAlarm and noCanCnt as five separate fields, strongly corroborating the official description of this register as a packed word of high/low-speed mode, "temp 70", long-press-reverse, no-CAN-timeout and throttle-lost-alarm bits. GDriver's 'temperature70' parameter independently confirms this same five-way packing, naming the same shared group — CAN timing, speed mode, reverse debounce, and throttle-loss protection — alongside its own two-bit thermal/auxiliary-I/O role; but GDriver's separate 'canDetectCount' parameter describes the no-CAN-timeout steps as 500ms per count for selectors 0-5 and 2ms per count above that, conflicting with this entry's '10s units' framing for the low byte. Treat the '10s units' claim with reduced confidence pending resolution; the packed five-field structure itself is now well corroborated.
notes: 高低速/温度70/长按后退/无CAN超时/油门丢失告警

name: Throttle auto-learn trigger and low-capacity speed limit
explain: Low byte = throttle auto-learn trigger/state (LearnThrottle), high byte = speed cap percentage applied when battery capacity is low (LowCapLimit, 0-80%). GDriver independently confirms both sub-fields by name: 'learnThrottle' as the fixed motor-drive command used during motor self-learning (explicitly not a throttle endpoint or riding limit), and 'lowCapacityLimit' as the lower battery-capacity breakpoint below which the low-charge limiting strategy applies its strongest reduction — implemented by reducing the active max line-current request (addr25) rather than a hard RPM cap, which refines this entry's 'speed cap percentage' framing toward a current-based limit (name match only, address unconfirmed).
notes: LearnThrottle/LowCapLimit | LearnThrottle=自学习油门(ProControlPage.cs:1740), LowCapLimit=限速极限电量(ProControlPage.cs:1741)

name: Mid-speed capacity-based speed cap
explain: Low byte = a speed cap value applied based on battery capacity (MiSpeedCap); high byte preserves a related SpeedLimitByCap value read back from the controller. GDriver independently confirms a matching 'midSpeedCapacity' field as the battery-capacity breakpoint at and above which the low-charge limiting strategy (addr158/addr204/addr206) has fully faded out and full availability returns — implemented, like addr204, via the maximum line-current request rather than a direct RPM cap (name match only, address unconfirmed; effect unverified).
notes: MiSpeedCap | MiSpeedCap=限速起始电量(MidSpeedCap label, ProControlPage.cs:1742)

name: Park coefficient, battery-signal type and min-speed-cap coefficient
explain: Low byte = a minimum-speed capacity coefficient (0-255); high-byte low nibble = park coefficient (0-15); high-byte high nibble = battery signal/chemistry type selector (one-wire/serial/CAN/lithium/lead-acid/LFP). Worthless models parkCoeff, batSel and minSpeedCapCoeff as three separate fields, corroborating the official description of this register as a packed park-coefficient / battery-signal-select / min-speed-cap-coefficient word. GDriver's parameter set independently matches all three sub-fields again: 'parkCoefficient' (Slow-down Park correction strength — larger values multiply the descent correction more strongly, on a non-linear scale on some controllers), 'batterySignal' (the battery communication source/chemistry profile selector), and 'midSpeedCapacityCoefficient' (the strongest low-charge current-limiting coefficient, applied at and below the addr205/addr204 capacity breakpoints) — a third independent name-match corroboration of this register's three-way packing, on top of the existing Worthless match.
notes: 驻坡系数/电池信号/MidSpeedCapCoeff

name: Re-acceleration ratio after regen
explain: Coefficient shaping how quickly torque resumes when the throttle is reapplied after a regenerative-braking event, per this entry's key name — though the official app's own field is labelled 'ReAcc' / 后退加速 ("reverse acceleration"), and GDriver independently matches a 'reverseAcceleration' parameter describing it as a reverse-mode acceleration-time setting that caps the acceleration step while a reverse-related operating mode is active, changing how quickly the reverse command builds rather than the final Reverse speed or current ceiling (addr41/201) — a materially different reading (reverse-drive acceleration, not post-regen throttle reapplication) from this entry's original 'regen acceleration ratio' framing. Treat the regen-specific framing with reduced confidence; 'reverse acceleration' is the better-supported reading (name match only, address unconfirmed).
notes: ReAcc | ReAcc=后退加速(ProControlPage.cs:1754)

name: One-wire comm protocol data bytes 0/1
explain: Two raw data bytes (DATA0 low byte, DATA1 high byte) sent as part of the one-wire dashboard protocol frame; exact meaning unconfirmed. GDriver independently confirms both sub-fields by name: 'oneWireData0' as a device code the controller uses to identify/compare against the matched display or peripheral on receive, and 'oneWireData1' as a data-mode selector — zero picks rolling/encrypted data, anything else picks fixed data — while noting that some firmware gives the raw values 254 and 255 their own extra handling on the receive side (name match only, address unconfirmed).
notes: DATA0/DATA1 | label: DATA0 / DATA1 (no localized string in .cs)

name: Rotor position sensor type
explain: Selects which type of rotor position sensor (Hall, incremental encoder, absolute encoder, resolver) the controller expects. GDriver independently describes a matching 'anglePosition' parameter for this same concept, additionally distinguishing 120-degree and 60-degree Hall-sensor profiles among the available options, and stresses a mismatch with the installed sensor can cause no-start, reverse rotation, rough launch, weak torque, high current, or motor faults (name match only, address unconfirmed).
notes: 位置传感器

name: Wheel radius and drivetrain gear/pulley ratio
explain: Low byte = drivetrain gear/pulley ratio (WheelRatio), high byte = wheel radius (WheelRadius); both feed the speed-display and speed-limit calculations. Worthless has separate aspectRatio and rimSize int fields; aspectRatio is a strong name match to the low-byte WheelRatio (轮胎扁平率 = tyre aspect ratio), while rimSize is a plausible but not certain match to the high-byte WheelRadius (tyre-sizing convention typically pairs rim diameter with aspect ratio and width, rather than a raw radius). GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address for two distinct sub-fields — 'aspectRatio' (tyre sidewall ratio) and 'rimDiameter' — strongly corroborating this entry's existing guess that the low byte is the tyre aspect ratio (matching WheelRatio/轮胎扁平率) and clarifying that the high byte, despite being labelled 'WheelRadius' in the official app, is actually the rim diameter in inches rather than a literal radius.
notes: WheelRadius/WheelRatio | WheelRadius=轮胎R(ProControlPage.cs:1903), WheelRatio=轮胎扁平率(ProControlPage.cs:1724)

name: Wheel/tyre width
explain: Tyre width value, used together with WheelRadius/WheelRatio for speed-display calculations (effect unverified).
notes: WheelWidth | WheelWidth=轮胎宽度(ProControlPage.cs:1723)

name: Speed/rate display calibration ratio
explain: Fine calibration multiplier for the speed or rate display, entered as a decimal and stored scaled by 1000. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms this exact address (id 'gearRatio') and the ×1000 storage scale, describing it as the drivetrain reduction ratio used together with wheel size and pole pairs for speed/distance calibration — it does not change the bike's physical sprockets or mechanical torque multiplication.
notes: RateRatio | RateRatio=传动速比(ProControlPage.cs:1902) | Worthless has a `gearRatio: Float` field — same physical quantity (a decimal drivetrain ratio) as this register's scale=0.001-quantized value, but no explicit numeric range is recoverable statically, so kept low.

name: One-wire comm idle/stop pulse timing and data-byte selectors
explain: Packed word: bits0-1 = idle pulse step (0.5/0.9/1.5/1.9ms), bits2-3 = stop pulse width (24/55/124/216ms), bits4-7 = which data byte is reported (Byte89Sel), high byte = ESQH square-wave-high time. GDriver's own parameter registry independently confirms both timing enumerations verbatim: 'oneWireIdle' lists the same four idle-pulse steps (0.5, 0.9, 1.5, 1.9 ms) and 'oneWireStop' the same four stop-pulse-width options (24, 55, 124, 216 ms) — strong corroboration of this register's bits0-3 packing, though GDriver does not address the Byte89Sel/ESQH high-byte fields (name match only, address unconfirmed).
notes: Idle/Stop/ESQH/Byte89Sel | Idle=步长(ProControlPage.cs:2668), Stop=停止间隔周期(ProControlPage.cs:2725), ESQH=特殊帧(ProControlPage.cs:1717), Byte89Sel=字节选项(ProControlPage.cs:2721)

name: Auto-learned input pin function result
explain: Write-only register used by the pin-function auto-detection wizard: low byte identifies which logical function is being assigned (P/BC/high-speed/low-speed/XH/seat/reset), high byte is the detected physical pin index found by watching for a state change.
notes: 识别功能脚
